headline: High risk: Roo Code can write and execute in the workspace while Khoj reads indexed notes, creating default-path prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Roo Code can read/write workspace files and use MCP, while Khoj reads indexed personal notes/files and supports web search/RAG. A shared filesystem or copied content can let attacker-controlled text from one agent influence the other. This is not proven by a documented bridge, so I avoid high, but the pathway is plausible in default developer workflows.
conditions: IF the two agents exchange files through a shared workspace or MCP channel, prompt injection becomes reachable.
IF Roo Code ingests Khoj-generated text as instructions, attacker-controlled content can steer tool use.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of untrusted notes into Roo Code prompts.
Keep Khoj and Roo Code on separate directories or workspaces.
Add a manual review step before copying agent output between tools.
Restrict MCP servers to trusted, provenance-tagged sources.
requires-engineering: add content provenance labels and instruction/data separation.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Khoj touches personal notes and indexed documents, and Roo Code can read/write workspace files and run browsers with broad network egress. If they share a workspace or the same user context, sensitive notes can flow into Roo Code outputs or browser/API traffic. The profiles do not prove uncontrolled exfiltration by default, so medium is the highest supported severity.
conditions: IF personal notes are copied into the VS Code workspace, Roo Code can access them.
IF Roo Code sends workspace content to configured APIs or browser sessions, notes may leave the local environment.
mitigations: Keep sensitive notes outside the shared workspace.
Use separate OS accounts or containers for the two agents.
Turn off browser/API features when handling private notes.
Review outbound requests before enabling networked tasks.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Roo Code has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, and broad network egress; Khoj reads files and maintains a shared index across clients. If both operate on the same workspace or indexed corpus, concurrent edits and index updates can race and corrupt state. Because Roo Code explicitly writes and modifies git state, the conflict is dangerous by default once co-located.
conditions: IF both agents point at the same repository or notes directory, concurrent writes can collide.
IF Khoj reindexes while Roo Code edits files, stale or conflicting state can be produced.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate workspace directory.
Pause Khoj indexing during Roo Code write sessions.
Avoid letting both agents modify the same git branch.
Use file locks or a single-writer workflow.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking and conflict detection.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Khoj is a retrieval/chat agent that can surface facts from notes, and Roo Code can act on outputs with shell, browser, and git capabilities. If Roo Code treats Khoj output as authoritative, a mistaken or injected retrieval result can cascade into code changes, commits, or external actions. The pair therefore has a default-path action-amplification risk.
conditions: IF Roo Code uses Khoj output without verification, incorrect facts can drive actions.
IF the workflow allows Roo Code to commit or browse based on retrieved text, errors can propagate outward.
mitigations: Require Roo Code to verify Khoj outputs against source files.
Use a checklist before any commit or browser action.
Limit Roo Code to read-only mode for retrieval-derived tasks.
Separate fact gathering from action execution.
requires-engineering: add citation and provenance checks before tool actions.

E_compliance.rationale: Khoj is designed for personal notes and indexed documents, while Roo Code handles source code and browser screenshots with broad network egress. If personal notes include regulated data and are moved into Roo Code's workspace or browser/API flows, retention and residency controls can diverge. The profiles do not show a specific certification mismatch, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated personal notes are copied into Roo Code-managed files or browser sessions, compliance scope expands.
IF the two agents retain logs differently, deletion/export obligations can diverge.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Roo Code tasks.
Review logging and retention settings for both tools.
Use separate storage locations for personal notes and code.
Disable browser workflows on sensitive datasets.
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion policies across both systems.
